page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a Cloud GPU server instance featuring a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, configured with 8 shared vCPUs across 4 physical cores. System memory totals 40.0 GB, providing 5.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard compute and memory tasks, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1786.68 and a multi-core score of 14175.12. PassMark CPU testing yields a score of 14090.9, while memory bandwidth tests show 784.94 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 88.57 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, the instance excels in LLM inference workloads, achieving top-tier performance with 9944.32 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a 135M model and 3147.67 tokens/sec on a 7B model.

The fractional GPU allocation offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated card. The shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff in environments requiring sustained, isolated CPU performance, though the local NVMe SSD provides fast storage access. This configuration is suited for small to medium LLM inference tasks, machine learning model evaluation, database operations, and GPU-accelerated web serving.
